opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building chips, modems and AI platforms; up 17% YoY.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling, legal costs and running the company; up 27% YoY.

opex.name: Other
opex.note: Restructuring and restructuring-related charges of $68M — substantially severance costs (10-Q); a one-time cost Qualcomm excludes from its non-GAAP results.

footerNote: Gross profit = revenues less cost of revenues. Qualcomm guided Q4 FY26 revenue to $9.7B–$10.5B.
oneTimers: The $68M 'Other' operating-expense line is restructuring and restructuring-related charges, substantially severance (10-Q) — excluded from non-GAAP results.

Most of the $1,014M investment and other income was paper gains: $726M of net gains on marketable securities and $149M on deferred-compensation plan assets (10-Q), plus $771M attributable to the QSI strategic-investment segment in Qualcomm's non-GAAP bridge.
Qualcomm flagged broad input-cost inflation — wafers, assembly, test, packaging and memory — and said pricing actions to offset it should benefit gross margins over time.
otherDetail: Investment and other income, net of $1,014M, less $178M of interest expense — a net $836M non-operating gain. The investment income was mostly gains on marketable securities and deferred-compensation plan assets.

segments.name: QCT
segments.note: The chip business. Inside it: Handsets $5,086M (−20% YoY), Automotive $1,588M (+61%), IoT $1,830M (+9%).

segments.name: QTL
segments.note: Licensing phone makers to use Qualcomm's patents — very high margin (69% pre-tax).

segments.name: Other and reconciling items
segments.note: QSI strategic investments and corporate items not in QCT or QTL; the difference between segment revenue and the reported total.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended Jun 28, 2026 (SEC EDGAR)

takeaways.text: Handset chip revenue fell to $5.09B as phone demand softened — the whole reason total revenue slipped 4% despite growth everywhere else.
takeaways.title: Handsets dragged

takeaways.text: Automotive chip revenue set another record at $1.59B and IoT grew 9% to $1.83B — Qualcomm's diversification beyond phones is working.
takeaways.title: Cars keep climbing

takeaways.text: Investment and other income of $1,014M — mostly securities gains — is why net income held at $2.0B even though operating income fell to $1.63B from $2.76B a year ago.
takeaways.title: Investments padded profit

verdict: Qualcomm's revenue slipped 4% to $9.9B as handset chips fell 20%, but record automotive sales and $1.0B of investment gains kept profit at $2.0B.
